mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 10% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 10% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases (PAYEMS) and unemployment decreases (UNRATE), it indicates a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rise but S&P 500 returns are positive during tightening.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI inflation leads to negative S&P 500 returns as inflation may erode corporate profits.
failure_condition: If CPI is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 indicates economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops below 90 but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Increased housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both HOUST and RSAFS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising unemployment (UNRATE) signals a slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises during late-cycle but S&P 500 returns are positive.
